question: Why did the bank start the scheme?
options: To stop farmers from taking loans
Because farmers spent their savings soon after the harvest
To compete with other banks in the town

group.title: Reading comprehension
group.setup: A small cooperative bank in a hill town noticed that many farmers withdrew all their savings right after the harvest and spent it within weeks. Instead of lecturing them, the bank started a simple scheme: any farmer who left a part of the harvest money untouched for six months received a slightly higher rate of interest and a free visit from an advisor. Within two seasons, deposits grew steadily, and farmers began to plan purchases of seeds and tools in advance rather than borrowing at high rates from local moneylenders. The manager later said that the extra interest mattered less than the visits, because farmers trusted advice given at their own doorstep.
